newsitem.title: UK: Ex BoE deputy says UK rates may need to rise.
newsitem.headline: Ex BoE deputy says UK rates may need to rise.

text.p: Howard Davies, who ends his tenure as Bank of England deputy governor on Friday to become head of Britain's new City regulator, said the UK economy may need a modest rise in interest rates.
"It is a rather difficult balance to set at the moment with the domestic economy booming away...but on the other hand, a very strong pound," he told BBC radio.
"A modest rise in interest rates may well be needed...now or later. That's certainly the market expectation."
Davies said the pound's rise was largely due to perceptions about European monetary union.

"A very strong part of the impulse behind sterling is that EMU may be coming but if it's coming it will be a broader EMU...and therefore possibly a weaker euro. Sterling has acquired a degree of safe haven status."
He said he was certain the Bank of England's monetary policy committee would ensure the government's 2.5 percent inflation target was met. "There is no disadvantage in having low inflation."
The committee meets to discuss monetary policy next week.

"Undoubtedly there is a perception that interest rates are rising here because the economy is moving ahead strongly and the markets can see that this is likely to require some rise in interest rates to dampen it down," Davies said.
He takes over as head of Britain's revamped Securities and Investment Board today.
